transcript: dear maria thank you for taking the time to meet with us last week i wanted to follow up on a few of the points we discussed because i think there was some confusion about the timeline and i would like to make sure we are on the same page before we go any further when we spoke you mentioned that your team needs the new onboarding flow to be live before the start of the next quarter we understand why that matters and we want to help you hit that date however as i explained during the meeting the integration with your existing human resources system is more complex than we originally estimated your system stores employee records in a format that we have not worked with before and our engineers need time to build and test a reliable connector if we rush that work there is a real risk that some employee records will be imported incorrectly which would create far more problems for your team than a short delay would with that in mind we would like to propose a phased approach in the first phase we would launch the onboarding flow with manual data entry so your new hires can start using it right away in the second phase which would follow about a month later we would switch on the automatic import once the connector has been fully tested against a copy of your real data we believe this gives you the best of both worlds because your team gets the new experience on time and you avoid the risk of corrupted records we are also happy to assign a dedicated support person to your account during the transition so that any questions from your staff are answered quickly please let me know if this approach works for you or if you would prefer to discuss other options i am available most afternoons this week if a call would be easier best regards aditya
reference: Dear Maria, thank you for taking the time to meet with us last week. I wanted to follow up on a few of the points we discussed, because I think there was some confusion about the timeline and I would like to make sure we are on the same page before we go any further. When we spoke, you mentioned that your team needs the new onboarding flow to be live before the start of the next quarter. We understand why that matters, and we want to help you hit that date. However, as I explained during the meeting, the integration with your existing human resources system is more complex than we originally estimated. Your system stores employee records in a format that we have not worked with before, and our engineers need time to build and test a reliable connector. If we rush that work, there is a real risk that some employee records will be imported incorrectly, which would create far more problems for your team than a short delay would. With that in mind, we would like to propose a phased approach. In the first phase, we would launch the onboarding flow with manual data entry, so your new hires can start using it right away. In the second phase, which would follow about a month later, we would switch on the automatic import once the connector has been fully tested against a copy of your real data. We believe this gives you the best of both worlds, because your team gets the new experience on time, and you avoid the risk of corrupted records. We are also happy to assign a dedicated support person to your account during the transition, so that any questions from your staff are answered quickly. Please let me know if this approach works for you, or if you would prefer to discuss other options. I am available most afternoons this week if a call would be easier. Best regards, Aditya

transcript: so i have been thinking a lot about how we run our weekly planning and i want to put down some thoughts before the retro on friday because i think we can do much better than we are doing right now the main problem as far as i can tell is that we spend most of the meeting talking about tasks that are already in progress and we leave almost no time to talk about what is coming next by the time we get to the new work everyone is tired people start to drift and we end up picking tickets almost at random that is not a good way to decide what the team should spend its week on i also noticed that the same three or four people do most of the talking and the newer folks rarely speak up even when they clearly have opinions some of them have told me privately that they do not feel comfortable interrupting which is a shame because they are often closer to the actual code than the rest of us so here is what i want to try first every status update happens in writing before the meeting in the shared channel so that nobody has to read out what they did on monday second we spend the first half of the meeting on the new work not the old work and we look at it in priority order so the most important items always get discussed while people still have energy third we go around the room once at the end and ask every person whether there is anything they disagree with so that quieter people have a guaranteed moment to speak fourth we keep the whole thing to forty five minutes and if we run out of time the remaining items wait until the next week rather than dragging the meeting on i know some of this will feel awkward at first especially the round at the end but i think it will make a real difference within a few weeks i am not attached to every detail and if reference: So I have been thinking a lot about how we run our weekly planning, and I want to put down some thoughts before the retro on Friday, because I think we can do much better than we are doing right now. The main problem, as far as I can tell, is that we spend most of the meeting talking about tasks that are already in progress, and we leave almost no time to talk about what is coming next. By the time we get to the new work, everyone is tired, people start to drift, and we end up picking tickets almost at random. That is not a good way to decide what the team should spend its week on. I also noticed that the same three or four people do most of the talking, and the newer folks rarely speak up, even when they clearly have opinions. Some of them have told me privately that they do not feel comfortable interrupting, which is a shame, because they are often closer to the actual code than the rest of us. So here is what I want to try. First, every status update happens in writing before the meeting, in the shared channel, so that nobody has to read out what they did on Monday. Second, we spend the first half of the meeting on the new work, not the old work, and we look at it in priority order, so the most important items always get discussed while people still have energy. Third, we go around the room once at the end and ask every person whether there is anything they disagree with, so that quieter people have a guaranteed moment to speak. Fourth, we keep the whole thing to forty five minutes, and if we run out of time, the remaining items wait until the next week rather than dragging the meeting on. I know some of this will feel awkward at first, especially the round at the end, but I think it will make a real difference within a few weeks. I am not attached to every detail, and if somebody has a better idea for any part of this, I would genuinely like to hear it. What I am attached to is the goal, which is that our planning meeting should actually help us plan, and that everybody on the team should feel that their voice counts when we decide what to build. Let me know what you think before Friday, either in the channel or by message, and we can try the new format starting the week after. If it does not work, we can always go back to the old way, but I would rather experiment than keep doing something that we all quietly agree is not working. Thanks for reading this far, and sorry it ran a bit long.

transcript: Dear Maria, thank you for taking the time to meet with us last week. I wanted to follow up on a few of the points we discussed, because I think there was some confusion about the timeline and I would like to make sure we are on the same page before we go any further. When we spoke, you mentioned that your team needs the new onboarding flow to be live before the start of the next quarter. We understand why that matters, and we want to help you hit that date. However, as I explained during the meeting, the integration with your existing human resources system is more complex than we originally estimated. Your system stores employee records in a format that we have not worked with before, and our engineers need time to build and test a reliable connector. If we rush that work, there is a real risk that some employee records will be imported incorrectly, which would create far more problems for your team than a short delay would. With that in mind, we would like to propose a phased approach. In the first phase, we would launch the onboarding flow with manual data entry, so your new hires can start using it right away. In the second phase, which would follow about a month later, we would switch on the automatic import once the connector has been fully tested against a copy of your real data. We believe this gives you the best of both worlds, because your team gets the new experience on time, and you avoid the risk of corrupted records. We are also happy to assign a dedicated support person to your account during the transition, so that any questions from your staff are answered quickly. Please let me know if this approach works for you, or if you would prefer to discuss other options. I am available most afternoons this week if a call would be easier. Best regards, Aditya
